summary: Rules restrict deletion to the password-provider moderator claim and preserve diary/intake isolation. The user explicitly chose a low-entropy shared password; this is not individual administrator authentication.

findings.issue: Anyone who knows or guesses the shared credential can delete public feedback; attribution and recovery are not provided. This behavior was explicitly requested after the risk was explained.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the shared credential when exposed, or migrate to individually authenticated moderators. Never embed it in public files.

findings.issue: The Firebase password identity retains standard self-account management capabilities outside Firestore rules, allowing a credential holder to disrupt shared authentication.
findings.recommendation: Restore or disable the dedicated identity through Firebase administration when necessary; deny comment deletes in rules for immediate revocation.
